The electric air taxi maker said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Ohio-based defense technology startup Resonant Sciences for roughly $500 million, giving Joby a dedicated defense business at a time when military spending and demand for autonomous aircraft are rising.

Resonant Sciences designs, manufactures, and delivers advanced radio-frequency and mission systems for U.S. national security customers. Once the acquisition closes, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business, bringing together its existing operations with Joby’s hybrid aircraft and autonomy technologies. The deal marks a significant shift for a company best known for developing electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs, for commercial passenger transportation.

The company that once raised venture funding to build an electric air taxi prototype is now preparing to own a defense technology operation with a major manufacturing footprint in Ohio. Joby is still betting on electric air taxis. With Resonant Sciences, it is making a second bet that the aircraft, autonomy, and engineering developed for that future can find a much nearer-term customer in defense.
